headline: EU Commission schedules special scientific-panel meeting on frontier AI risks after reported loss-of-control investigations
summary: A European Commission press release dated 9 October 2026 announced a special meeting of the AI Act Scientific Panel on frontier AI safety and security risks. In a Spanish-language follow-up published 12 October, the Commission says the meeting addressed recent loss-of-control incidents, model monitorability and recursive self-improvement; it summarizes four recommendations, including governance of internal-model risks, stronger incident-investigation capacity, international information sharing and scrutiny of training techniques that reduce monitorability. The Commission also says it will send combined questions to developers as it investigates incidents. The sources do not identify the incidents or models, publish the questions, or establish that the recommendations became binding policy. This is a first-party account of advisory work, not independent incident verification. In an October 28 press briefing, the Commission said it had received replies to expired information-request deadlines across two AI Act RFI tracks sent to more than 30 companies and was assessing them; some deadlines were extended. The automatically generated transcript names no recipients and gives no findings.
